canonical_data: skill documents, role definitions, and the generated paper MCP server files in the user’s workspace
current_repo_note: The repository ships as a skill package rather than a standalone product: role documents and stage prompts the host coding agent executes, plus helper scripts that do the enforced verification work. The host, not this repository, runs the coordination loop; the skill’s own orchestration document states that a role description alone is not a running agent. A legacy-cli tag preserves an earlier shell-based CLI that the current tree no longer ships.
strengths: Enforced verification rather than assertion: verify_workflow.py checks phase order, agent separation, and hashes, and verify_mcp_server.py launches the built server and verifies tool inventory, schemas, and acceptance calls, so a failing build stops instead of being described
Peer-reviewed and Nature-published with open access, and the evaluation is concrete: 593 of 599 generated tools passed validation and 91.2 percent of 300 benchmark questions were answered correctly
The output is portable by design: every paper becomes an MCP server any compatible agent or LLM can connect to, demonstrated by three running Spaces (AlphaGenome, Scanpy, TISSUE)
weaknesses: No continuous integration, no releases, and a single test file; the verification gates execute only inside a host-agent run, so nothing independently validates the skill’s own code

The headline evaluation claims are paper-attested, not repository-verifiable: only three of the reported seventy-four-agent corpus are published as Spaces, and the benchmark figures live in the paper, not in a reproducible harness in the repository
It is a workflow for a host, not a standalone system: without Claude Code, Codex, or another skill-reading agent, the repository ships prompts and helper scripts that run nothing on their own
why_it_matters: The first peer-reviewed system that turns a paper itself into an executable artifact: a paper and its codebase become a validated MCP server any agent can query, with results checked against the paper’s own outputs before the server ships.
